summary: 제안 논문은 open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization이라는 다운스트림 과제를 정식화하고 OV-AVEBench에서 segment-level localization을 평가하는 반면, 기존 논문은 여러 모달리티를 하나의 공유 임베딩 공간에 결합하는 범용 멀티모달 표현 학습을 다룬다. 다만 제안 논문은 기존 논문의 pretrained ImageBind 통합 임베딩 공간과 인코더 구성을 특징 추출 backbone으로 직접 활용하므로, 문제 설정은 다르지만 방법 측면에서는 일부 핵심 기반을 공유한다.

differentiation_suggestions: Our work uses the pretrained ImageBind space as a backbone, but it is developed for the specific downstream task of open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization rather than for learning a general joint embedding across modalities. Accordingly, our method focuses on predicting explicit event categories for seen and unseen events in test videos.

Unlike the prior work, our training-free baseline uses the consistency between audio-text and visual-text similarities as a task-specific inference rule for localization. This makes the shared embedding space serve a concrete prediction mechanism instead of only a representation-learning objective.

Our approach further introduces lightweight temporal layers to model temporal relations within the audio and visual modalities for event localization. This temporal modeling component addresses segment-level dynamics that are not specified in the prior work's general multimodal embedding framework.
related_work_draft: The prior work (Girdhar et al., arXiv, 2023) learns a unified embedding space that aligns multiple modalities through image-centered training and provides the pretrained ImageBind backbone used in our work. In contrast, our work studies open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization, building task-specific temporal modeling and prediction procedures on top of that shared multimodal representation.

differentiation_suggestions: Our work uses the pretrained ImageBind embedding space as a feature backbone, but targets open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization rather than learning a general-purpose joint embedding space. In particular, our task requires explicit category prediction for both seen and unseen events at the segment level in test videos.

Our training-free baseline operates by comparing the consistency between audio-text and visual-text similarities within the shared embedding space. This differs from the prior work, which establishes cross-modal alignment during pretraining rather than defining a localization-oriented prediction rule on top of that space.

Our method further introduces lightweight temporal layers implemented with a stack of standard Transformer blocks to model temporal relations within audio and visual modalities. This temporal modeling is applied for downstream event localization, whereas the prior work describes modality encoders for representation learning without a task-specific temporal localization module.
related_work_draft: The prior work (Girdhar et al., arXiv, 2023) learns a unified multimodal embedding space by aligning multiple modality encoders to image embeddings. Our work builds on this representation as a pretrained backbone, while focusing on open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization with segment-level prediction of seen and unseen events.

summary: The proposed paper and the prior work are related through the use of ImageBind's unified multimodal embedding space, but they address different problems. The proposed paper formulates open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization with seen/unseen event localization on OV-AVEBench, whereas the prior work studies general-purpose multimodal representation learning by aligning multiple modalities in one shared embedding space. The proposed paper therefore builds on the prior work's representation backbone while adding task-specific temporal modeling for downstream localization.

The proposed paper overlaps with the prior work in backbone representation learning, especially the shared multimodal embedding space and encoder/projection design. However, their scope and objective differ because the proposed paper targets segment-level open-vocabulary localization, while the prior work evaluates broad zero-shot classification and retrieval across many modalities.

differentiation_suggestions: Our work uses the prior work's unified multimodal embedding space as a feature backbone, but it targets open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization rather than general multimodal representation learning. In particular, our task requires explicit prediction and localization of both seen and unseen events in test videos.

Unlike the prior work, which evaluates broad zero-shot classification and retrieval across multiple modalities, our work is built around OV-AVEBench with segment-level manual annotations for audio-visual events. This makes the evaluation focus on segment-level localization rather than general embedding transfer across datasets.

Our work extends the reused multimodal backbone with lightweight temporal layers to model temporal relations within audio and visual modalities for localization. This temporal modeling component is introduced for downstream event localization, whereas the prior work does not present a task-specific temporal relation module.
related_work_draft: Our work builds on the prior work of Girdhar et al., arXiv, 2023 by using IMAGEBIND's unified multimodal embedding space as a backbone for audio, visual, and text features. Unlike the prior work, which studies general-purpose multimodal alignment, our work focuses on open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization with task-specific temporal modeling and segment-level evaluation.
